mintAuthority.summary: cNGN's verified native issuance surface is the Africa Stablecoin Consortium issuer account for the CNGN credit asset on Bantu. The Bantu ledger is the stated source of truth for supply; the authored EVM deployments are destination representations under the Bantu lock-and-mint model, while the Solana deployment is conservatively treated as a representation because independent native liability and reconciliation are not proven. No separate issuer-side economic cap or timelock was evidenced. The issuer-linked August 31, 2026 ISAE 3000 reserve examination reconciles circulating cNGN across eight named chain liabilities, but neither its accountant signature nor the management stamp is dated, so no dated whole-supply reconciliation covering the destination representations is admitted.

review.evidence: The cNGN FAQ and Bantu Foundation case study identify Bantu as the native issuance ledger and state that Bantu remains the source of truth for total supply while bridge contracts lock Bantu cNGN and mint equivalent destination representations. The Bantu issuer account and CNGN asset were re-read at ledger 34,127,652 on 2026-08-16. No dated whole-supply attestation reconciling Bantu issuance to all destination representations was accessible. The native posture remains unbounded-adverse; reconciliation was unknown at that review. The Solana Token-2022 program can mint its deployment, but the reviewed primary sources do not prove whether that deployment is an AMTP representation or an independently reconciled native liability chain. It is therefore not used to support native issuance. Both questions the boundary migration raised are decided here rather than left open: the Solana deployment is conservatively classified as a representation because independent native issuance is unproven, and Bantu's absence from the route inventory is a catalog chain-registry gap rather than an unreviewed issuer fact. Neither is an open question about this issuer's mint authority. ODR-A6 lane R reconciliation review 2026-09-01: https://cngn.co/transparency states 'We conduct monthly audits on reserve funds' but links only two smart-contract security audits (Frank Castle, January 2026; Hashlock, July 2026) and renders its live reserve widget at zero across every metric as of 2026-08-31. No reserve report link, no attestation PDF and no token-supply figure appear anywhere on the page. /attestation, /reserves, /proof-of-reserve and /sitemap.xml each return 404, docs.cngn.co carries API documentation only with no attestation or reserve page in its navigation, and a Wayback CDX sweep of cngn.co/* shows the domain has never hosted an attestation or reserve document. It only hosts auditReportBg.png and totalReserve.png interface chrome. The Bala Isah Garba & Company ISAE 3000 engagement remains secondary-press-only: the newest report referenced anywhere is October 2025, the press piece that describes the monthly series states the reports are reachable via cngn.co while supplying no URL, and no Nigerian SEC or CBN publication of a cNGN reserve attestation exists (the only regulatory artefact is the 2024 SEC Approval-in-Principle under ARIP). reconciliation is therefore recorded as the positively-established 'none' rather than left at the unverified 'unknown' (MINT-LADDER 9.32); no supply or reserve figure is admitted from any of this. Follow-up 2026-10-19: the 2026-10-05 mechanism review (W3R39) retracted the unreachable-report finding; the issuer-linked August 31, 2026 ISAE 3000 report is publicly reachable and, re-read from the PDF on 2026-10-19, its Table 3 lists eight named chain liabilities (Bantu, Assetchain, Base, BNB Chain, Celo, Ethereum, Polygon, Solana) totalling NGN3,329,961,223.91 circulating cNGN against a NGN3,550,845,048.39 reserve book. Its practitioner signature and management stamp carry no signing or publication date, so it is not admitted as a dated reconciliation; the reconciliation field is left unchanged pending a mint-authority re-review.

noLocalIssuance.rationale: Every deployment currently authored in the catalog is a destination representation: the five EVM routes are supported by the Bantu lock-and-mint architecture, and Solana is conservatively classified as a representation because independent native issuance is unproven. Native issuance is verified on Bantu, but bantu is not a registered catalog chain identifier and therefore cannot be authored as a route or contract row within this scoped migration. This explicit exception prevents the untracked Bantu issuer control from implicitly targeting a destination route.
